title: Compact-collapse heuristics and canvas-clip guardrails for charts, tables, and modal layering
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: High-density dashboard views and canvased charts can overflow, clip awkwardly, or produce inconsistent stacking across Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox when viewport width is reduced and modals open. This causes visual artifacts (half-pixel strokes, shadow cutoffs), keyboard focus traps to break, and interactive table rows to become hard to target on touch devices. Goal: define compact-collapse heuristics for panels, standardized canvas clipping rules for charts and embeddable canvases, and a layering/z-index guardrail for modals/tooltips that behaves consistently across browsers and input modes. Deliver a set of prototypes, handoff-ready specs, and measurable acceptance criteria for engineering to implement in runtime-1.19/console-2026.03.
acceptance_criteria: Dense dashboard rows collapse to a predictable 2-tier distribution (primary/secondary) under 960px with no content overlap
Canvas-based charts render consistent axis hairlines and shadows across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox at devicePixelRatio 1 and 2
Modal stacking and tooltip z-order follow a deterministic rule set; keyboard focus trap and aria-hidden toggles work when multiple overlays are present
Touch hit targets for table rows and inline controls meet 44px minimum after density adjustments
Prototype validated in Chrome 116+, Safari 16+, Firefox 116+ with documented browser-specific workarounds
deliverables: Figma prototype (compact + expanded states) with annotated constraints and responsive breakpoints
Interactive CodePen shim demonstrating canvas clip & shadow fixes
Handoff spec PDF with CSS variables, recommended z-index scale, and JS heuristics for collapse thresholds
Acceptance test checklist and cross-browser validation matrix
design_decisions: Use semantic collapse tiers (primary/secondary) instead of purely pixel-driven shrinking to preserve core info density
Prefer CSS transform + overflow:hidden for canvas containers to avoid layout thrashing and preserve GPU compositing on Safari
Introduce a 10-level z-index scale (base, panel, overlay, modal, modal-top, toast) and require engineering to expose it as CSS tokens
Avoid CSS calc() reliance for critical clipping; instead provide explicit pixel fallbacks for older WebKit engines
Tooltips should render in a dedicated overlay root to avoid stacking context collisions with transformed parent nodes
